pageTitle: 2026 USTA Foundation Opening Night Gala provides young people with opportunities to unlock their excellence

bodyText:
The USTA Foundation’s Opening Night Gala at the 2026 US Open raised $2.7 million Sunday evening, directly fueling transformative programs that provide tennis, education and mentorship opportunities to young people from under-resourced communities nationwide. In 2025, this support helped over 233,000 young people access no-cost tennis, education, and mentorship programs, as well as college scholarships and high-performance training support through more than 270 community organizations to prepare them for life on and off the court.

Award-winning journalist and longtime supporter of the USTA Foundation, Gayle King, served as gala host, while Yesim Philip, USTA Foundation Advisory Board Member, served as gala committee chair. International Tennis Hall of Famers Bob and Mike Bryan served as honorary Gala co-chairs and joined world-renowned auctioneer Dale Johannes for a live auction where supporters bid on unique experiences. ESPN was the event’s Presenting Sponsor.

2017 US Open champion, former world No. 3, and Olympian Sloane Stephens was honored with the USTA Foundation’s Serving Up Dream Award. Stephens has leveraged her elite tennis career into a powerful platform for social change through the Sloane Stephens Foundation. Established in 2013, her foundation empowers thousands of young people in under-resourced communities across Compton, Calif., Fresno, Ca., and Miami Gardens, Fla., by providing a blend of academic enrichment, mentorship, mental health support, and athletic training.

Riley Woodson and Sloane Stephens pose with guests and the “Serving Up Dreams” USTA Foundation award at the USTA Foundation Gala. Photo by Michael Le Brecht II/USTA.

Stephens’ significant impact off the court has earned her national recognition, including being named one of TIME Magazine’s 100 Most Influential People in Philanthropy and receiving the 2025 ESPY Awards' Muhammad Ali Humanitarian Award, solidifying her legacy as an influential leader and advocate for youth empowerment.

“We believe that all young people, no matter where they live or who they are, should have the opportunity to unlock their full potential,” said Ginny Ehrlich, USTA Foundation CEO. “Together with our generous supporters and partners, we aren’t just broadening access to tennis; we are championing the next generation of leaders and equipping them with the tools they need to thrive, wherever their journeys take them.”

The USTA Foundation works year-round to support its flagship National Junior Tennis & Learning (NJTL) network, co-founded in 1969 by tennis and humanitarian icon Arthur Ashe, Charlie Pasarell and Sheridan Snyder. Ashe’s widow, Jeanne Moutoussamy-Ashe, attended the gala, along with other supporters including actor Orlando Bloom, fashion icon Vera Vang, US Olympic Gold Medalist Lindsey Vonn, two-time Super Bowl champion Justin Tuck, actress Kate Walsh, actor Da’Vinchi, journalist Katie Couric and many more.
